resolution_needed: Le Grand Cléré is retained as the canonical producer display name while Domaine Grand Cléré and Boisson Vivante remain sourced trade/name forms rather than separate producers.
statement: François Blanchard works from Château du Perron in Lémeré; public sources use Le Grand Cléré or Domaine Grand Cléré for the winegrowing identity and Boisson Vivante as a trade/signature presentation.

Le Grand-Cléré is described as an approximately three-hectare clay-and-flint site around 110 metres on the Touraine plateau, planted for roughly fifty years to Sauvignon, Cabernet Sauvignon and Cabernet Franc.

resolution_needed: Seek the Ecocert certificate or certificate directory before assigning certification dates or scope beyond the association member declaration.
statement: The Vins S.A.I.N.S. member page reports four planted hectares, manual harvest, organic farming, no synthetic products and Ecocert certification; CARTA treats the certification as source-attributed pending certificate-level reconciliation.
The 2022 ordinary A Table ! bottling is documented as Vin de France, 100% Sauvignon, sourced from Le Grand-Cléré; it remains distinct from A Table ! Grains Dorés.

For 2022, importer technical material describes hand destemming, about one month of skin maceration, gentle wooden-press pressing, six months in barrique, unfiltered bottling and no added SO2; the association analysis reports total SO2 below 10 mg/L.

scope_notes: The producer's separate 'third generation winery' wording conflicts with its own fourth/fifth-generation labels, so CARTA keeps the named dates and omits a generation ordinal.
statement: Weingut Günther Steinmetz traces production to 1900; Günther took over the family business in 1957, Stefan assumed winemaking leadership in 1999, and Sammie and Stefan have run the winery together since 2014.

The estate describes hand harvesting and sorting, avoidance of fertilisers, herbicides and insecticides, and cellar work without added selected yeasts, fining agents, acid/deacidification agents or animal proteins, with spontaneous fermentation in large wood or steel; CARTA does not infer organic certification.

The 2018 Pinot Noir Unfiltriert used estate-holding fruit from Burgen, Kesten and Mülheim plus fruit from unnamed friendly growers in Brauneberger Klostergarten and Piesporter Falkenberg; it was 60% destemmed, spent 12 months in used barrique and was bottled unfiltered.
The 2019 Pinot Noir Unfiltriert used estate-holding fruit from Kesten and Mülheim, was 70% destemmed, spent 24 months in used barrique and was bottled unfiltered.

resolution_needed: Do not infer Qualitätswein, Landwein, Deutscher Wein, Prädikatswein or another legal category from the reported 'No AP' wording alone.
statement: Mosel Fine Wines records the 2018 Pinot Noir Unfiltriert as 'No AP'; this is retained as source wording and does not resolve the wine's exact German legal classification.

The German Wine Institute treats Spätburgunder and Pinot Noir as names for the same grape variety; CARTA therefore keeps the bottle wording Pinot Noir while governing Spätburgunder on the existing Pinot Noir grape identity.

Domaine de la Bergerie's first-party chronology begins with Marie-Scolastique Bouhiron's 1961 purchase, records Anne joining in 2010, Anne and Marie taking the reins in 2018, and Amaury joining vineyard work in 2024; stale importer copy conflicts on dates, surname and leadership status.
The producer reports a 27-hectare vineyard and certified organic farming since the 2016 vintage; older trade pages reporting 35 or 36 hectares are not used as the controlling area figure.

scope_notes: The producer page heading and breadcrumb say 2022 while image/HTML metadata say 2021; CARTA treats the visible product content as the 2022 release and preserves the CMS inconsistency as a research note.
statement: The 2022 Clos de la Bergerie is documented as 100% Chenin, Coteaux du Layon, from the source-described La Bergerie site at Champ-sur-Layon on clay-schist, with slow pressing, light settling, indigenous-yeast fermentation and élevage in tank.

Coteaux du Layon is an AOP/AOC sweet white-wine designation based on Chenin; the governing framework requires overripe fruit and manual selection, while noble rot is characteristic but not a universal requirement of every base-designation wine.

resolution_needed: Do not infer enclosure, cadastral identity, ownership, exact boundary or WITHIN_APPELLATION status from the word Clos or the source line La Bergerie.
statement: The producer identifies the wine's source as 'La Bergerie — Champ-sur-Layon'; CARTA records a source-described site without fabricating geometry or parcel-law containment.

scope_notes: The importer states exceptions for DC, MA, MD, NC and VA; the claim is observation-scoped and not treated as timeless exclusivity.
statement: Martine's Wines states that it is the exclusive U.S. importer for Domaine de la Bergerie except in DC, MA, MD, NC and VA.
